building.name: Wisconsin Commercial Building Code (Wis. Admin. Code chs. SPS 361 to 366), adopted in Milwaukee Code of Ordinances s. 262-01
building.edition: 2021 International Building Code with Wisconsin changes (DSPS inserts headed 'September 1, 2025 Wisconsin Commercial Building Code, SPS 361 - SPS 366'; state pack)
building.local_amendments_note: The city's adopting section takes ch. SPS 362 (new construction) and ch. SPS 366 (additions, alterations, change of use and repairs) 'as amended' and adds two International Building Code sections, 907.1.1 and 414.1.3. Neither is in the plumbing-fixture chapter (Chapter 29) and their text was not read. No city change to toilet counts, stalls or interior finish was found. State law gives Wisconsin one uniform commercial building code (state pack, DSPS Act 270 FAQ).
building.effective: 2025-09-01 for the state code edition, per the heading of the DSPS inserts (not confirmed on a DSPS page; state pack). The city's adopting section was recreated by Common Council file 220693, passed 2022-09-20.
building.quote: 262-01. Adoption of State and International Building Codes. 1. NEW CONSTRUCTION. The city of Milwaukee adopts ch. SPS 362, Wis. Adm. Code, as amended, s. 907.1.1, International Building Code, and s. 414.1.3, International Building Code as part of this code. 2. ADDITIONS, ALTERATIONS, CHANGE OF USE, AND REPAIRS. The city of Milwaukee adopts ch. SPS 366, Wis. Adm. Code, as amended, s. 907.1.1, International Building Code, and s. 414.1.3, International Building Code as part of this code.
building.quote_source: City of Milwaukee Common Council file 220693, 'An ordinance relating to increasing fees for plan examinations, updating building code procedures and adopting portions of the Wisconsin administrative code and International Building Code', Part 10; status Passed, 2022-09-20. Text as passed, not the current consolidated code.

plumbing.name: Wisconsin Plumbing Code (Wis. Admin. Code chs. SPS 381 to 387), a state-written code; Milwaukee Code of Ordinances ch. 225 (Plumbing and Drainage) holds the city's permit and licensing rules
plumbing.local_amendments_note: Chapter 225 of the Milwaukee Code could not be opened, so the section that adopts the state plumbing code and any city additions were not read. What was read: s. 225-3-1 as amended in 2013 (plumbing permits) and s. 225-31-1 as amended in 2022 (gas piping follows NFPA 54 / ANSI Z223.1, 2015). In Wisconsin the toilet count is in the building code (SPS 362.2902), not the plumbing code (state pack).
plumbing.quote: 225-3. Plumbing Permits Required. 1. ISSUANCE. No permit for plumbing shall be issued by the commissioner to any person not duly licensed, registered and bonded. Permits issued shall be subject to the rules and regulations of the commissioner, and it shall be unlawful to do any plumbing without a permit with the exception of work regulated in sub. 3 and work exempted under s. 200-24-1.5.

fixtures.basis: Milwaukee's adopting section (s. 262-01, as recreated in 2022) takes ch. SPS 362 'as amended', which is where Wisconsin's toilet-count changes sit (SPS 362.2902), and adds only International Building Code sections 907.1.1 and 414.1.3, which are outside the plumbing-fixture chapter. Wisconsin has one uniform commercial building code (state pack). The state pack's worked examples stand. The current text of chapter 262 was not read on the city's site, so a later city change cannot be ruled out from the code itself.

permit.required_quote: 200-24. Permit Required. 1. REQUIRED. No person may erect, construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, improve, convert to new uses, raze or demolish any building or structure, nor install therein any equipment, occupy and use any building, structure, equipment or premises or cause the same to be done or commence any excavation on any premises without first obtaining a permit from the commissioner and paying the fee as prescribed by this code. The list does not name toilet partitions or compartments. Items f-8 ('similar finish work'), f-9 (replacement of interior wall finishes) and f-10 (minor repair the commissioner accepts) are the nearest; whether any covers a partition replacement is not stated. restrooms_city.quote: Resolved, By the Common Council of the City of Milwaukee, that the City expresses its commitment to creating gender-inclusive restrooms and other facilities, such as locker rooms and changing rooms, in properties owned or operated by the City; and, be it Further Resolved, That the City urges other municipalities and entities that control places of public accommodation throughout the city and surrounding areas to create gender-inclusive restrooms and other facilities [...]
restrooms_city.note: No city ordinance on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms in private buildings was found (one web search; title search of the city's legislation system for 'restroom'). Common Council resolution 191168, passed 2019-11-26, covers buildings the city owns or operates and only urges others to follow; it sets no rule for private buildings. Chapter 109 of the Milwaukee Code (equal rights), which the resolution cites, was not read. This is 'none found', not 'none exists'.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Milwaukee job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Wisconsin rules Milwaukee enforces.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Milwaukee breweries, manufacturing plants, schools and medical offices, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Wisconsin's building rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. Milwaukee adopts them as the state writes them. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Milwaukee requires a permit from the Department of Neighborhood Services to alter or repair a building or install equipment in it, unless the work is on the city's exempt list. The list covers "painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinet or countertop installation, and similar finish work" and repairs the department's commissioner judges minor, without naming toilet partitions. Ask the Department of Neighborhood Services whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of Milwaukee Department of Neighborhood Services
page.install_rule: Building permits in Milwaukee come from the city's Department of Neighborhood Services, which also reviews plans for commercial buildings in place of the state. Check local contractor licensing or registration with the department before work starts. Wisconsin does not license contractors for commercial work at the state level: state licensing covers one- and two-family dwelling contractors and certain trades, such as electrical and HVAC. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: Wisconsin has no state contractor license for commercial work, so check what the city asks of contractors with the Department of Neighborhood Services.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Wisconsin repealed its own wage law for public jobs in 2017, so set wage rates apply only on federally funded work, under the federal Davis-Bacon Act. For a carpenter on building work in Milwaukee County that rate is $45.46 an hour plus $31.52 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7.9% in Milwaukee: 5% state, 0.9% Milwaukee County and 2% city.
page.buyers_extra: - **Breweries, taprooms and food plants:** solid plastic or stainless steel for rooms with wet floors and regular washdown.

Checked 2026-11-24.

- Milwaukee permits and exempt work: Milwaukee Code of Ordinances ss. 200-24-1 (permit required) and 200-24-1.5 (exceptions), as amended by [Common Council file 121804](https://milwaukee.legistar.com/gateway.aspx?m=l&id=/matter.aspx?key=37197), "A substitute ordinance relating to exceptions to department of neighborhood services permit requirements", passed December 17, 2013, read in the city's legislation system. - Sales tax in Milwaukee: Wisconsin Department of Revenue, [Tax Rates](https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/pcs-taxrates.aspx) (5% state; Milwaukee County 0.9% from January 1, 2024; City of Milwaukee 2% from January 1, 2024). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Milwaukee County carpenter rate on federally funded building work: [federal wage determination WI20260001, modification 1, May 18, 2026](https://sam.gov/wage-determination/WI20260001/1). Checked 2026-11-24.

notes: city.milwaukee.gov blocks automated reading (403), so no page of the city's website was read: the city facts come from ordinances as passed, read in the city's legislation system (Legistar), and from state pages. Check in a browser that s. 200-24-1.5 (permit exceptions, as passed in 2013) and s. 262-01 (code adoption, as passed in 2022) still read the same in the current Milwaukee Code of Ordinances.

To confirm by phone before launch: whether a like-for-like replacement of toilet partitions in a commercial restroom needs a Milwaukee permit, and whether adding stalls does (Department of Neighborhood Services, Permit and Development Center; web-search summaries of city documents give 414-286-8210 and 809 N. Broadway, not read on a page, so the number is not in the page text).

Contractor rule: still the neutral line from the local-rules file (low confidence, phone-call item). Chapter 200 and the city's licence chapters could not be read. One fact was read: plumbing permits go only to a person 'duly licensed, registered and bonded' (s. 225-3-1), which doesn't concern partition installers.

City restroom rules: none found for private buildings. Common Council resolution 191168 (passed November 26, 2019) commits the city to gender-inclusive restrooms in buildings it owns or operates; it is a resolution, not a rule for buyers, so it stays out of the page text. Chapter 109 (equal rights) was not read.
Sales tax: 7.9% applies in the part of the city in Milwaukee County, which includes downtown. The city also reaches into Washington and Waukesha counties, where the county part differs.

The wage rate is the union carpenter rate in the federal determination for Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Washington and Waukesha counties; it applies on federally funded work only. Any City of Milwaukee wage rule on city contracts was not looked for.
The two extra building-code sections Milwaukee adopts (International Building Code 907.1.1 and 414.1.3) were not read; they are outside the plumbing-fixture chapter.
The four building types in the lead and the buyers bullet on breweries, taprooms and food plants are editorial, not sourced.
